newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra wins approval for asthma inhaler.
newsitem.headline: Astra wins approval for asthma inhaler.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said on Monday that it had won its first approval for its asthma inhaler, the Oxis Turbuhaler, which will be launched in Sweden early 1997.
The company said in a statement that it expected to have pan-European approval for the asthma treatment in 1997 and the product would be available in the United States and Japan in a few years.
"This new product has significant potential within the fast growing bronchial therapy market for Astra," the company said.
Astra said the market for such inhalers was worth 13.6 billion crowns in 1995 and was projected to increase to 21 billion crowns by the year 2000.
"Long acting inhaled bronchodilators will probably represent 40 percent of these sales," Astra said.
The Oxis Turbuhaler is designed to be used in conjunction with Astra's largest selling current inhaler range, the Pulmicort Turbuhaler," it said.
